## [`sceptre`]{style="font-size:60px;"}

`sceptre` is an R package for single-cell CRISPR screen data analysis, emphasizing statistical rigor, massive scalability, and ease of use.

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R-CMD-check](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre/check-standard.yaml?branch=main&cacheSeconds=30)](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre/actions?query=workflow%3AR-CMD-check+branch%3Amain)

<!-- badges: end -->

## Optional nuisance fitting backends in this fork

The fitting methods for gene expression (`Y | Z`) and gRNA propensity
(`X | Z`) can be selected independently:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Native structured Poisson and logistic fitting, inspired by pysceptre.
obj <- set_analysis_parameters(
  obj,
  response_fit_method = "pysceptre",
  grna_fit_method = "pysceptre"
)

# Full glmGamPoi response fitting with the structured logistic backend.
obj <- set_analysis_parameters(
  obj,
  response_fit_method = "glmGamPoi",
  grna_fit_method = "pysceptre"
)
```

`response_fit_method = "pysceptre"` uses native RcppEigen Poisson IRLS and
the existing SCEPTRE conditional negative-binomial size estimator and clamp.
`"glmGamPoi"` instead fits both NB coefficients and dispersion with
`glmGamPoi::glm_gp()`. The default response method remains `"sceptre"`.
The gRNA choices are `"glm.fit"` (default), `"fast_logistic"`, and
`"pysceptre"`; gRNA fitting is used only for CRT analyses.

The native structured methods exploit mutually exclusive indicator columns
without constructing a cells-by-squared-covariates array. Genes and targets
are fitted independently; chunk size controls loading and scheduling rather
than the numerical fit. Treatment-plus-NT analyses prepare each target's
own cell population. The methods require no Python runtime. Unsafe numerical
fits fall back to `stats::glm.fit()` with the same family. Per-target gRNA
backend, convergence, and fallback information is available through
`get_grna_fit_diagnostics(obj)`; new response caches carry a
`fit_diagnostics` attribute.

The structured assembly is adapted from
[Broad Institute pysceptre](https://github.com/broadinstitute/pysceptre/tree/7adaa9f5fda12e0cf87df972c8fe73b73ef13e7d),
with native conditioning, line search, and fallback safeguards. These choices
do not alter the selected association-test or resampling algorithm, but
numerical changes in nuisance estimates can affect downstream results.
Speed depends on the covariate design and workload. A reproducible fitting
microbenchmark is available at `inst/benchmarks/pysceptre-glm.R`.

## Experimental shared preparation for CRT SPA

The existing `crt_spa_always_fast` method can reuse target propensity
transformations and small gene information matrices within one analysis:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
options(sceptre.crt_spa_shared_preparation = TRUE)
```

The default is `FALSE`. This optimization applies when response fits share
the outer-regression cell population. It retains the exact Bernoulli CGF,
information statistic, solver controls, and empirical fallback rules. Other
testing modes keep their existing implementation. Preparations are run-local
and are not saved in the response-fit cache. Analysis phase timings include
all preparation costs and report preparation counts and retained geometry size.
The prepared native call retains the R owners of read-only target arrays and
gene weights, avoiding full-length copies; its feature matrix remains pair-local.
Prepared six-column designs (including the intercept) use a fixed seven-moment
kernel and retain the
accepted cell tilts for the final stable KL calculation, guarded by an exact
state match. Other dimensions use the generic evaluator. No bounded gene-vector
cache is retained.

## v0.10.0: `sceptre` at massive scale

`sceptre` v0.10.0 represents another a major upgrade to the `sceptre` software. We have integrated `sceptre` with [`ondisc`](https://timothy-barry.github.io/ondisc/), a companion R package that facilitates large-scale computing on single-cell data. `sceptre` now supports the analysis of single-cell CRISPR screen data out-of-core on a laptop or distributed across hundreds of processors on a computing cluster or cloud.

`sceptre` v0.10.0 includes the following updates:

-   Support for disk-backed `sceptre` objects, enabling the analysis of data too large to fit in memory
-   A `sceptre` [Nextflow pipeline](https://github.com/timothy-barry/sceptre-pipeline), enabling the deployment of `sceptre` across hundreds of processors on a cluster or cloud
-   An updated [e-book](https://timothy-barry.github.io/sceptre-book/) containing new sections about at-scale `sceptre` and the statistical methodology underlying `sceptre`
-   New functionality for plotting and inspecting gRNA-to-cell assignments
-   A comprehensive suite of unit tests, which verify the correctness of the code
-   More detailed man pages (including runnable examples) and minor bug fixes

You can see our [RECOMB poster](https://timothy-barry.github.io/poster_recomb_2024.pdf) for more information about this update.

## Featured publications

-   [Barry et al., 2024](https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-024-03254-2). "Robust differential expression testing...". *Genome Biology*.
-   [Barry et al., 2024](https://timothy-barry.github.io/biostatistics_2024.pdf). "Exponential family measurement error models...". *Biostatistics.*
-   [Morris et al., 2023](http://sanjanalab.org/reprints/Morris_Science_2023.pdf). "Discovery of target genes and pathways...". *Science*.
-   [Barry et al., 2021](https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-021-02545-2). "SCEPTRE improves calibration and sensitivity...". *Genome Biology*.

`sceptre` also recently was featured in a [10x Genomics analysis guide](https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/single-cell-crispr-screen-analysis-with-sceptre).

## Bug reports, feature requests, and software questions

For bug reports, please open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre/issues). For questions about `sceptre` functionality, documentation, or how to apply it to your data, please start a discussion under [Q&A](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre/discussions/categories/q-a).
